requirements.quote: As a transport protocol, MQTT is concerned only with message transmission and it is the implementer’s responsibility to provide appropriate security features.
requirements.condition: When MQTT is used in an environment requiring security controls
requirements.required_behavior: The implementer would provide security features outside MQTT's message-transmission function.
requirements.why_checkable: The text does not define which security properties or mechanisms are appropriate, so it supplies no objective pass/fail behavior for an implementation.

requirements.quote: The CONNECT Packet contains Username and Password fields.
requirements.condition: For the MQTT CONNECT Packet model
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must define and be able to represent the Username and Password fields of CONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT encoder, decoder, or packet representation can be inspected for both named fields without asserting that they are present in every packet.

requirements.quote: Implementations can choose how to make use of the content of these fields.
requirements.condition: When an implementation receives Username or Password content in CONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: The authentication use of that content may be implementation-defined.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A conformance check must not require one particular authentication mechanism solely from this statement.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's policy can select local, external, operating-system, or other authentication handling without violating this protocol-level permission.

requirements.quote: Implementations passing authentication data in clear text, obfuscating such data elements or requiring no authentication data should be aware this can give rise to Man-in-the-Middle and replay attacks.
requirements.condition: When authentication data is clear text, merely obfuscated, or absent
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation would account for Man-in-the-Middle and replay risks.
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase “should be aware” specifies no required mitigation, observable state change, or acceptance criterion, so the constrained behavior is incomplete.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol is not trust symmetrical: it provides no mechanism for the Client to authenticate the Server.
requirements.condition: When only the MQTT protocol mechanisms defined here are used
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must treat Server authentication as unavailable at the MQTT protocol layer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Client must not claim that core MQTT alone authenticates the Server.
requirements.why_checkable: The MQTT handshake and packet fields can be inspected for absence of a Server-authentication mechanism, independently of external transports such as TLS.

requirements.quote: There are valid TLS cipher suites that include a NULL encryption algorithm that does not encrypt data.
requirements.condition: When a TLS cipher suite using a NULL encryption algorithm is negotiated
requirements.required_behavior: The connection's application data must be treated as unencrypted rather than confidential by virtue of TLS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not represent a NULL-encryption TLS connection as providing data encryption.
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated cipher suite can be inspected for a NULL encryption algorithm and the implementation's privacy classification checked.

requirements.quote: To ensure privacy Clients and Servers should avoid these cipher suites.
requirements.condition: When Clients and Servers intend TLS to ensure privacy
requirements.required_behavior: They should avoid negotiating cipher suites that use a NULL encryption algorithm.
requirements.why_checkable: TLS configuration and negotiated cipher suites can be checked for exclusion of NULL encryption when privacy is an explicit objective.

requirements.quote: This would not provide privacy for other properties of the Application Message such as Topic Name.
requirements.condition: When an application independently encrypts only the contents of its Application Messages
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must treat non-content properties such as Topic Name as not protected by that content encryption.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not claim that encrypting Application Message contents also makes Topic Name private.
requirements.why_checkable: A captured PUBLISH Packet can be inspected to distinguish encrypted payload contents from the separately exposed Topic Name.
